text.p: Swiss shares recoiled from losses in the second half of the session after U.S. producer price data, a firming U.S. dollar and early Wall Street gains provided support for the market.

But trading was rangebound and generally lacking direction for much of the session, dealers said. Dollar sensitive stocks were in demand while banks were mostly lower. Nestle first half-year figures and U.S. consumer price data due on Friday were keeping investors on the sidelines.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index advanced 8.3 points, or 0.23 percent, to end at 3,687.2 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index rose 5.52 points, or 0.23 percent, to 2,361.99.
Most-active Union Bank of Switzerland bearer shares were among the more conspicuous losers of the day. The stock lost 21 francs, or 1.79 percent, to end at 1,150.
Banks were pressured by rumours about reductions in second half profit forecasts by foreign brokers, dealers said.
Swiss Bank Corp fell 1.75 francs to 231, while CS Holding was flat at 121.50.
Nestle edged up one franc to 1,423. Market expectations for the company's first half profit were in a range of 1.2 billion and 1.4 billion francs.
Pharmaceuticals profited from U.S. dollar strength. Ciba registered shares added 15 francs to 1,573. Swissair, Surveillance and Holderbank were also seen underpinned by the firming U.S. currency.
